vo: Right now, a message from Earth takes a full day to reach this spacecraft.

label: 49 years earlier
vo: Forty-nine years earlier, Voyager 1 lifted off from Florida, built for a mission of about five years.
It launched during a rare line-up of the outer planets that happens about once every 175 years.
Each planet's gravity flung it faster, like a slingshot. Free speed.
On board, a golden record with music and greetings from Earth, in case anyone ever finds it.
It runs on a nuclear battery that's slowly fading, so engineers keep switching instruments off to save power.
Its radio signal is about as strong as a fridge light bulb. Yet giant antennas on Earth still hear it.

label: Now
vo: And now it's so far away, light itself needs a whole day to get there. Nothing we've built has ever gone farther.
Every message we send it... is already a day old when it arrives.
